newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rain disrupts last stages of French maize harvest.
newsitem.headline: Rain disrupts last stages of French maize harvest.

text.p: Rain is disrupting maize combining operations in France's southwest and in the east, threatening to push back the end of the harvest by about two weeks to mid-December, local crop analysts said on Monday.
In the Aquitaine region, where most of the country's maize is produced, the harvest is now 95 percent complete but steady rain over the last three weeks has kept farmers away from the fields.
"It has been raining for almost three weeks and 20,000 hectares still need to be harvested on the southern patches of Bearn," one analyst said.
Analysts predicted possible yield loss on patches that have not yet been harvested but said the damage should be marginal.
Local ONIC officials said that they were maintaining their estimates for 1996 regional yields at 9.3-9.4 tonnes per hectare against 8.0 tonnes last year.
The delivered crop may reach 2.9 million tonnes, up 30 percent from last year.
In eastern France the harvest is now 90 percent complete, but rain and snow have held up combining operations in the Haut-Rhin area.

Local ONIC officials are now forecasting regional yields of 8.9 tonnes per hectare, unchanged from last year. The delivered crop may jump 14.9 percent to 1.2 million tonnes, mostly because of a higher sowing area.
The crop suffered from dry conditions in the summer while cool temperatures in autumn slowed down crop development.
